- Overestimate prices after strong positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or shows recent sharp declines; model underreacts to bearish signals.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after sentiment shifts; adjust for delayed reaction.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs/lows, fails to smoothly revert to historical mean unless sentiment confirms trend.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model overfits short-term noise; reduce forecast volatility in such periods.
- High sentiment + high price = model overconfident; reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% if sentiment > 0.5 and price > 78.
- Low sentiment + low price = model underconfident; increase forecast by 5–10% if sentiment < -0.5 and price < 72.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves after 3+ consecutive negative sentiment days; model often misreads reversal signals.
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model tends to overreact; cap forecast increase at +10% from prior peak.
